Summary of what I heard:
- Primary requirement: predictable latency for inference requests (low tail/p99 behavior) for payment-insights workloads.
- Biggest concern: "noisy neighbor" effects on shared clusters causing latency spikes during peak batch jobs.
- Regulatory/data separation: preference for isolation of customer data and auditability (retain logs for 12+ months).
- Primary candidates we discussed: Hosted API (fast TTV), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Private VPC/on-prem (full control).

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below (high level) and Marissa will follow with the detailed SLO table and isolation architecture.

High-level SLO/latency expectations (text gen, 50-200 tokens, Nucleus-style batching):
- Hosted API: p50 ~ 40-70 ms, p95 ~ 180-350 ms, p99 ~ 400-700 ms (depends on model & sequence length). Designed for low friction but can show higher tail under cross-tenant burst loads.
- Dedicated capacity: p50 ~ 25-45 ms, p95 ~ 80-160 ms, p99 ~ 120-250 ms. Dedicated GPU pools + reserved slots reduce jitter and tail; numbers assume mid-sized open models and warm KV cache.
- Private VPC / on-prem: depends on customer infra; with same HW + tuning you can expect better or comparable p95/p99 to Dedicated (we provide tuning guidance and kernel selection).

Noisy-neighbor mitigation strategies we use / recommend:
- Physical and logical isolation: Dedicated uses separate GPU pools (no cross-tenant scheduling) and optional host pinning for highly sensitive customers.
- Reservation & soft quotas: reserved slots for critical low-latency tenants to prevent eviction under bursty usage.
- Prefix/KV cache isolation: per-tenant KV caches to avoid cold starts and cross-tenant cache eviction.
- Autoscaling + burst buckets: capacity buffers to absorb short spikes without impacting reserved throughput.
- Fallbacks & graceful degradation: automatic routing to smaller models or lower-quality quantized variants when tail latency threatens SLOs, with configurable policies.
- Observability: token-level latency tracing, per-route p95/p99 dashboards, and alerting for noisy-neighbor patterns.

I've attached the short SLO doc (redwood-slos-v1.pdf) — it contains examples across model families and recommended guardrails. Marissa, can you add the baseline numbers for the Dedicated footprint we typically provision for FinPay-style workloads and confirm audit/logging behavior for Private VPC?

Next steps: lock in Tue 16 11:00 PST for tech deep-dive. I'll send calendar invite once you confirm.

— Priyom

Hi Alice / team — quick follow up from the infra/solutions side (short bullets):

- Dedicated baseline we recommend for FinPay PoC: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool) with per-tenant slot reservation; expected p95 ~ 90-140 ms for 50-200 token gen in our standard config.
- Isolation: Dedicated = separate Kubernetes/GPU nodepools (no shared scheduling). Private VPC = full network & control-plane separation; logs can be forwarded to your Splunk/ELK via secure connector.
- Audit & KMS: Private installs support customer KMS/HSM. Dedicated (hosted) supports customer-managed keys using KMS integrations and detailed audit logs retained per contract.
- Runbook: on noisy-neighbor detection we throttle lower-priority queues, spin burst capacity, and notify both infra owners + SRE.

I've attached the SLO cheat sheet (redwood-slos-v1.pdf) and an initial mutual action plan. Confirming Tue 16, 11:00 PST works for me — we'll bring our infra lead and solutions engineer.
